items.title: How Marriott Is Investing in the Maldives to Win Indian Travelers
items.summary: The Maldives has always been an easy sell for Indian honeymooners. The opportunity for hotels now is to get these travelers to come back for short family breaks, birthdays, or long weekends.

items.title: Delta and Amex GBT Test One-Click Status Enrollment for Corporate Travelers
items.summary: Both companies are betting that the one-click enrollment capabilities for Delta SkyMiles will boost engagement with business travelers.

items.title: Americans Paused. Canadians Pivoted. Europe’s Marketing Has to Change.
items.summary: Americans and Canadians have stopped traveling like one market. Whether a European destination runs North America from New York or has a team in Toronto, the ones that plan for each market separately stand to take the growth.

items.title: Fuel Doubled. Five Counterparties Now Decide Which Airlines Absorb It.
items.summary: Jet fuel prices doubled in 2026, and the question for every airline is who captures the margin that remains. Increasingly, the answer sits with counterparties: manufacturers, unions, premium travelers, airports and the banks behind co-brand cards.

items.title: Why Everyone Wants to Give You 10% Back on a Hotel
items.summary: Ten percent back has become a common hotel reward, and what a company can afford to pay depends on what the customer is worth to it after checkout.

items.title: Booking Holdings Plans to Fund New AI Startup Vayo With $100 Million
items.summary: Booking already has tools that organize trips. Vayo's proposition is that AI can turn the itinerary into something more: a system that learns how you travel, watches the entire trip, and starts working before you ask.

items.title: Portugal Picks Lufthansa Over Air France-KLM for TAP Stake
items.summary: Lufthansa gets its gateway to Brazil, but Lisbon still holds the controlling stake – at least for now.
